desc:
Ecom Swift LLC adds WooCommerce subscriptions and B2B setup to your store: recurring billing, paid memberships, wholesale pricing or multi-vendor selling, configured in your own account and tested for every type of customer.

## What is an advanced WooCommerce build?

An advanced WooCommerce build is a store whose business model goes beyond one-off retail sales. It adds rules for who can buy, what they pay, how often they are billed and who gets paid. WooCommerce handles the basics well, and the advanced models are added with extensions, custom settings and careful configuration on top of it.

The four models we set up most often are recurring subscriptions, paid memberships, wholesale or B2B pricing with approved buyers, and multi-vendor marketplaces.

## Why the rules matter more than the plugin

Installing an extension takes minutes. Making it behave correctly takes planning. A subscription that renews at the wrong price, a wholesale buyer who sees retail prices, or a vendor who can edit another vendor's listings are the kind of faults that cost trust and money, and they usually appear only after real customers arrive.

Each model creates new customer types, and every type needs its own path through the store. A subscriber needs a clear account page with renewal dates. A wholesale buyer needs a login and a price list. A vendor needs a dashboard. If any of these paths is missing or confusing, support requests grow and customers leave.

## How the right model affects revenue and retention

Recurring billing turns a single sale into a relationship. A customer who renews automatically keeps buying without being persuaded again, so the store depends less on constant new traffic. The same logic applies to memberships, where access to content, discounts or perks gives people a reason to stay.

Wholesale pricing opens a second sales channel with larger orders from fewer buyers. A marketplace lets other sellers fill your catalog while you earn a commission. In each case the mechanism is the same: the store matches how your customers actually want to buy. What you earn still depends on your product, your audience and your pricing.

## What a well-built advanced store includes

- Written pricing, renewal or commission rules that everyone on your team can read.
- Products configured for the chosen model, such as subscription plans or role-based price tiers.
- Separate customer roles with the right access, tested with real test accounts.
- An account page that shows members and subscribers their plan, next payment and order history.
- Customer emails for each event, such as signup, renewal, approval or a payment problem.
- Failed payment handling, so a declined card triggers a clear retry and notice instead of silence.
- Approval steps for wholesale buyers or new vendors before they can see prices or list products.
- Commission calculation and payout reports for marketplace stores.
- Notes or an admin guide so your team knows how to manage the model day to day.

## How we work

We start with a planning conversation. You tell us how the model should work, and we write the rules down: who qualifies, what each group pays, when renewals happen and what happens when something fails. You approve that document before we touch the store.

Then we configure and connect the right tools in your own WooCommerce install, apply the rules to your products and build the account page changes. Next we create test accounts for each customer type and walk each one from signup to renewal or order. Any rule that behaves unexpectedly gets fixed before handover.

The Basic package covers one model on a small set of products. Standard widens that to more of your range with role-based pricing, member account changes, customer emails and failed payment handling. Premium covers larger builds such as multi-vendor setups, vendor signup, commission rules, payout reports and a role testing report.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide your pricing and renewal rules on paper before any setup begins.
- Start with one model and add a second only when the first works.
- Test every customer type with its own test account.
- Check how taxes and payouts are handled in your region with an accountant.
- Keep a short admin guide for anyone who joins your team.

**Avoid:**
- Stacking several overlapping extensions that all change prices.
- Launching without testing what happens when a card is declined.
- Showing wholesale prices to visitors who are not approved.
- Letting vendors publish products without any review step.
- Changing renewal prices on live subscribers without telling them.

## Who this is for

This service suits a food or supplies brand that wants customers to reorder on a schedule, a manufacturer that sells to retailers and needs separate wholesale pricing, and an organizer who wants paid members to reach exclusive content or perks. It also suits a founder building a small marketplace where several makers sell in one store.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of the model you want, the products or plans it applies to, and any pricing tiers you already have. Tell us which payment gateway you use. We work in your account as an administrator user created for us, so we never need your password. Extension licenses, where an extension is paid, are bought by you directly from the maker.
